Alright. So there's a lot of good, and a lot of not so good elements going on here. I'll try to be brief and hit the main points of what I thought. (Written with the vocalist in mind, since that's who I assume is posting.)

Presentation

I personally did not like the video for Striking Gold. I was left with a very bad taste in my mouth mostly due to the poor acting on the vocalist's part. That said, I don't expect her to be good at lip-syncing being an amateur artist. My advice in this area is to release live performances, (like you guys have for your other songs,) or to come up with visuals that deliver the feel you're going for in your music, without having to actually preform yourselves. By removing yourselves completely from your Striking Gold video, I would've been much more focused on the music, rather than the acting.

I'm going to assume you're familiar with them, but Mumford & Sons did a great series of videos of abstract visuals. Obviously they have way higher production quality, but the feel of the video I linked is still similar to your Striking Gold video. What you're aiming to achieve as a new artist is not to put out videos that make you seem experienced, but put out music that resonates with your first time listeners. You should be pouring 110% into your sound, and doing minimal work for the videos. A great thing to do is put out lyric videos, because they require minimal effort but keep the viewers focused on the content.

I very much liked your two live performances with the whole band. I feel that preforming music live is a better way to connect with your audience, and really show what you can do. Oftentimes I find myself enjoying live versions of performances better than the produced ones. A youtuber who does great live performances is the singer/songwriter Daniela Andrade.

Vocals

Not much to say here. You have a very good voice for this genre of music. That said, I was left a little wanting from your mixing. Because the instrumentals are not very complex with your music, you voice needs to be at the forefront of the soundscape. In your Striking Gold video, your voice felt very muted, when I would much prefer to have it the major focus of the music. It was slightly better in the live performances, mostly due to the live instruments being subdued as well. I do understand that working with limited production equipment can hinder the sonic qualities of your music.

One thing I will say is that you should try to push your voice to its limits. Not everybody has a wide range that they can hit, but staying in a one octave range the entire can start to make your listeners bored with your "sound." You have a very beautiful voice, and I would like to hear much more of what you can do. No need to worry that much about that yet since you don't have a sizable catalog of music yet. More just food for thought.

Overall Sound

Going to try to leave out my personal taste in this part, since taste is completely subjective. From the three songs you have on your youtube channel, it seems like your sound is heading towards an indie-folk sound. What you want to do if you're going to stay in this genre is differentiate your sound from the pack. Right now there isn't anything that stands out in your music except the grooves. Every band is has limiting factors, be it vocal range, skill with instruments, or limits of creative thinking. It's up to you to find the area that your band excels at and push that as far as it can go. If you have a talented songwriter, expand on the lyricism; tell a story, make a concept album. If you have an amazing bass player, drop some dirty baselines; give the listeners something they can groove to. Every popular band in the indie-alternative genre has something that they do better than others. The band Alt-J is my favorite example of a band who found something they do that nobody else does, and using that to build a foundation to their music. You want people to hear you and within 5 seconds immediately know it's your band. Give them a sound they can remember.

Conclusion

I really like where your sound is heading. While Striking Gold was bland and mostly forgettable, I found Oh Mercy enjoyable to listen to, and found myself wanting to hear more. It is my hope that your band will continue to expand on the sound you are fostering, which I think has potential. Thank you very much for posting, as it was a joy to critique. I hope something I've said helps you to make music that I enjoy even more.
